# Configuration

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-config-profiles.py. Do not edit. -->

66 settings across 7 roles. 10 weaken a control when moved off their default and are marked **unsafe**. 11 are secrets and belong in a secret backend, never in an image or a compose file.

## Precedence

Highest wins:

1. An explicit argument passed to the SDK constructor
2. An environment variable
3. `xcp.toml` in the working directory
4. The setting's documented default

A setting the code cannot honour is not silently ignored. The gateway refuses to start when `XCP_PRIVATE_PEER_CIDRS` is set and the egress guard is unavailable, and when `XCP_SECURITY=1` and `xcpsec` is missing, because an operator who believes a control is active and is wrong is worse off than one who got an error.

## Profiles

| Profile | Purpose | Pinned | You supply |
|---|---|---|---|
| `evaluation` | A single node for trying XCP against endpoints you have not vetted. | 5 | 0 |
| `enforce` | A production single-site node. | 9 | 4 |
| `private-federation` | Independent nodes across datacentres in one trust domain. | 14 | 10 |

Files: `deploy/profiles/*.env`.

### Deliberately absent from every profile

- **`XCP_ALLOW_INSECURE_PEERS`** — development only; declare XCP_PRIVATE_PEER_CIDRS instead, which is narrower and cannot re-admit link-local or cloud metadata.

These are absent rather than pinned to a safe value, because a profile is a file operators copy and edit, and putting the name in front of them makes the unsafe edit a one-character change.

## Every setting

### gateway

| Setting | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `XCP_A2A_ACCEPT` | `0` | Accept delegated tasks from peer gateways at /v1/a2a/accept. OFF by default: a node that accepts them is executing work on another datacentre's say-so, which an operator should decide deliberately rather than inherit from an upgrade. A ticket is still only admitted from a verified peer, in this node's cluster, naming this node, within its expiry, for the exact task committed to. |
| `XCP_A2A_MAX_HOPS` | `3` | How many boundaries one delegation may cross. Matches the federation's transitive-trust cap, for the same reason: beyond it nobody in the chain can reason about what they are part of. The originator sets the budget in the ticket and no hop can raise it. |
| `XCP_A2A_TIER_CEILING` | `A2xH2` | The most authority a cross-boundary delegation may carry HERE, whatever the originating gateway asserted. The asserted tier is narrowed leg by leg against this, so authority can only shrink at a boundary. The default is the top of the lattice, meaning 'whatever the origin verified'; an operator who wants delegated work capped lower sets e.g. A1xH1. The gateway refuses to start on a value it cannot parse, because a ceiling nobody can read is a ceiling that does not apply. |
| `XCP_ADMIN_TOKEN` | — | **secret** — Bearer token for /admin/* and the full peer list. When unset the administrative endpoints are DISABLED rather than open — an admin surface that defaults to open is worse than one that does not exist. Compared in constant time. |
| `XCP_CACHE_TTL` | `30` | Seconds to cache a verification result. Longer means a revocation takes longer to bite. |
| `XCP_CLIENT_CA_BUNDLE` | — | CA bundle that must have signed an agent's client certificate for the mtls registrar. Distinct from XCP_PEER_CA_BUNDLE, which anchors PEER NODES rather than agents; a deployment may well use one CA for both, and should have to say so. |
| `XCP_ENGINE` | `0` | Enable the self-hosted decision engine: a local classifier that estimates a request's complexity and risk so cheap requests can take a cheap route. Advisory ONLY — it cannot change whether a request is permitted, in either direction, and a refusal never cites it. Unlike XCP_SECURITY the gateway does NOT refuse to start when this is 1 and the engine is unavailable, because an absent optimisation is not an absent control: it degrades to silence and the node takes the route it would have taken anyway. |
| `XCP_ENGINE_BUDGET_MICROS` | `2000` | Per-request classification budget. A tier whose typical cost exceeds what remains is skipped rather than attempted, because a classifier that adds latency has failed at its own job. |
| `XCP_ENGINE_FASTTEXT` | — | Path to a fastText model for the engine's linear tier. Absent, that tier abstains; see `xcp engine --diagnose`. |
| `XCP_ENGINE_SETFIT` | — | Path to a SetFit model for the engine's semantic tier. At ~25ms it exceeds the default classification budget, so it also needs XCP_ENGINE_BUDGET_MICROS raised deliberately. |
| `XCP_GATEWAY_ID` | `gw-local` | Identifier stamped on audit records and forwarded downstream as XCP-Verified-By. |
| `XCP_GLOBAL_CONCURRENCY` | `256` | Node-wide in-flight request cap. |
| `XCP_GLOBAL_RATE` | `120000` | Node-wide cost units per minute, independent of any caller's tier. |
| `XCP_LIMIT_FAIL_OPEN` | `0` | **unsafe** — Serve traffic if the limiter itself fails. Turns any limiter bug into an abuse bypass; only for private deployments behind another limiter. |
| `XCP_MAX_UPSTREAM_CREDENTIAL` | `8192` | Maximum bytes the gateway will relay in XCP-Upstream-Credential. The value is never read, logged or stored; this bounds what the pass-through will carry. |
| `XCP_OIDC_ISSUER` | — | Issuer URL for the oidc registrar. Required when XCP_REGISTRAR=oidc; without it nothing would actually be checked. |
| `XCP_POLICY` | — | Path to a policy document. When set, every governed call is evaluated against it and the gateway REFUSES TO START if the document cannot be loaded — a policy you asked for and did not get is a control you believe you have. |
| `XCP_POLICY_APPROVED_DIGEST` | — | Digest of the policy an auditor approved. The gateway compares it against the policy it is actually enforcing and warns on divergence, which is what gives the policy adjudicative standing rather than resting on the operator's word. |
| `XCP_POSTURE` | `enforce` | **unsafe** — enforce \| observe. Observe logs decisions without blocking them — for onboarding an endpoint you have not vetted, never a steady state. |
| `XCP_PROFILE` | `development` | development \| production. The production profile refuses to start unless enforce posture, an external verifier, hardening, rate limiting, an admin token and secure peering are all in place — a profile that is claimed and not enforced is worse than one never claimed. |
| `XCP_RATE_LIMIT` | `1` | **unsafe** — Abuse controls. Setting 0 on a node reachable by strangers makes it an open relay. |
| `XCP_REGISTRAR` | — | What vouches for an agent when a session opens: none \| mtls \| oidc \| chain. Each justifies a different maximum agent tier — none A0 (self-asserted, development only), mtls and oidc A1 (your own CA or IdP issued it), chain A2 (a registry a peer who does not trust you can check). Empty infers chain when XCP_VERIFY_URL is set and none otherwise. The production profile refuses 'none'. |
| `XCP_REGISTRAR_CEILING` | — | **unsafe** — Override the maximum agent tier this node's registrar justifies, e.g. A2. Raising it above the registrar's default is permitted and PUBLISHED in the node record, because a node asserting A2 on the strength of its own CA is making a claim its peers are entitled to discount. Lowering it needs no announcement. |
| `XCP_RESIDENCY_SITES` | — | Comma-separated sites where a relayed tool call's data may be processed, e.g. 'eu-west-1,eu-central-1'. When set, a peer outside is INADMISSIBLE rather than merely expensive — a jurisdiction is not a quantity you can be compensated for crossing. A peer that declares no site fails this: not knowing where a peer is is not the same as it being somewhere permitted. Empty means no residency constraint. |
| `XCP_SECRET_*` | — | **secret** — Prefix for the env secret backend, e.g. XCP_SECRET_CONNECTORS_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID. Development only. |
| `XCP_SECURITY` | `0` | Enable the xcpsec argument firewall. The gateway REFUSES TO START if this is 1 and xcpsec is unavailable, rather than running with a control you asked for silently absent. |
| `XCP_TOOL_FALLBACK` | `0` | Ask a peer for a tool this node cannot reach. OFF by default: a call leaving for another datacentre is a different data path than the one configured in XCP_UPSTREAMS, and the operator should choose it. With it on, an unknown server is routed to a peer that advertises it, preferring the nearest site and refusing any site XCP_RESIDENCY_SITES does not permit. |
| `XCP_TOOL_RELAY` | `0` | Serve tool calls on a peer's behalf at /v1/tool/relay. OFF by default: relaying spends THIS node's vendor credential on another datacentre's say-so. A relayed call is admitted exactly as a cross-boundary delegation is — verified peer, this node's cluster, naming this node, within expiry, for the exact call committed to — and runs at the tier narrowed under this node's ceiling. Enabling it also advertises this node's upstream server names to peers. |
| `XCP_UPSTREAMS` | `{}` | **required** — JSON map of name to MCP url, e.g. {"research":"https://.../mcp"}. Empty means every a2t call 404s. |
| `XCP_UPSTREAM_RELAY_CREDENTIAL` | — | **secret** — The credential this node presents upstream when serving a relayed call. It belongs to THIS node — the asking datacentre never holds or sees it, which is the reason to centralise egress at all. Prefer a vault:// reference. |
| `XCP_VERIFY_URL` | — | External verifier. Unset uses in-memory bindings, which is fine for one node and insufficient for a federation. |

### server

| Setting | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `REQUIRE_VERIFIED` | `1` | **unsafe** — Refuse calls that did not arrive through a gateway. Setting 0 lets anyone reach the tools directly, bypassing every control. |
| `XCP_SERVER_NAME` | `research` | Name this server answers to in XCP_UPSTREAMS. |

### verifier

| Setting | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `CHAIN_ID` | `8453` | Chain id bound into EIP-712 domains. A signature is only valid for the chain it was signed against, so a mismatch here rejects every mandate with an unhelpful error. |
| `CHAIN_RPC` | — | EVM RPC endpoint. Unset means in-memory verification. |
| `SESSION_REGISTRY` | — | Deployed SessionRegistry address. Required with CHAIN_RPC. |
| `SESSION_REGISTRY_ABI` | — | Path to an ABI override. Defaults to the generated artifact. |

### node

| Setting | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `XCP_ALLOW_INSECURE_PEERS` | `0` | **unsafe** — Permit peering over plain HTTP and to ANY private or loopback address. This disables the SSRF guard on the peer-record fetch and is for local development only; on a reachable node it lets a caller make the gateway fetch internal services. The production profile refuses to start with it set. For a private federation use XCP_PRIVATE_PEER_CIDRS, which is the scoped half of this and does not waive TLS. |
| `XCP_CLUSTER_AUTHORITY` | — | Address of the key allowed to sign this cluster's charters. Without it a node accepts any correctly-signed charter naming its cluster id, so anyone could mint one. Set it on every node. |
| `XCP_CLUSTER_CHARTER` | — | Path to the signed cluster charter this node federates under. The charter commits to the member set with a Merkle root and carries no roster, so it can be distributed to every node without publishing who is in the cluster. A closed cluster refuses any peer whose membership proof does not verify against THIS charter's root — never against one the peer supplied. Unset means no cluster, and peering is bilateral. A charter that does not verify stops the node: starting without it would leave a closed cluster accepting any peer, which is what it exists to prevent. |
| `XCP_CLUSTER_MEMBERSHIP` | — | Path to THIS node's own membership proof, issued by the cluster authority. Published in the node record so peers can verify this node against their own charter. The node refuses to start if the proof does not verify, or if it is a proof for a different node — which catches a membership file copied from another datacentre. |
| `XCP_CLUSTER_MIN_EPOCH` | `0` | Refuse a charter below this epoch. Raising the epoch is how a member removal takes effect, so an operator pinning the floor stops a rolled-back charter file re-admitting a node that was removed. Set it to the epoch you currently expect. |
| `XCP_NODE_CERT_FOOTPRINT` | — | keccak256(DER(cert)) of the certificate currently served. scripts/rotate-cert.py maintains this. |
| `XCP_NODE_DOMAIN` | — | Domain this node claims. Must match where the record is served. |
| `XCP_NODE_KEY` | — | **secret** — Long-lived node identity key. LOSING THIS IS UNRECOVERABLE: the node loses its identity and every attestation any peer made about it. Back it up offline before first use. |
| `XCP_NODE_OPERATOR` | `anonymous` | Operator name published in the node record. |
| `XCP_NODE_RECORD_PUBLIC` | `0` | **unsafe** — Serve the FULL node record to anyone, even in a closed cluster. A closed cluster gates its record by default — publishing the topology of a federation only members may join is incoherent, and gating also means a removed member loses discovery and not just peering. Set this for a node that must stay publicly discoverable: a public-facing gateway inside a private organisation, or one under external monitoring. It publishes this node's id, gateway URL, operator and seed peers. |
| `XCP_NODE_SITE` | — | This node's datacentre, region or zone — an opaque label you choose, e.g. 'dc1-dublin' or 'eu-west-1'. Peers prefer local routes over crossing a site boundary and apply their own residency rules against it. Unset means this node has no locality, so every peer is equally near and nothing is preferred. Published in the node record (a peer cannot observe it) and withheld from the reduced one. |
| `XCP_NODE_URL` | — | Public gateway URL published to peers. |
| `XCP_PEER_CA_BUNDLE` | — | PEM bundle of the certificate authorities that sign THIS federation's peers. When set it REPLACES the public trust store for peer-record fetches and certificate-footprint retrieval — and for those only, so upstream tool calls keep public trust. Needed for a private federation using an internal CA: chain validation ran against the system store and failed before the footprint binding was reached. A mixed deployment concatenates the public roots it needs into the same file, which keeps the trust decision in one auditable place. An unreadable or empty bundle stops the node starting; falling back to the public store would leave the operator believing peers are verified against their own CA. |
| `XCP_PRIVATE_PEER_CIDRS` | — | **unsafe** — Comma-separated internal ranges that may hold federation peers, e.g. "10.40.0.0/16,fd00:dc1::/48". Without this a peer on a private address is unreachable, which made a private federation across datacentres impossible to run under the production profile. Narrower than XCP_ALLOW_INSECURE_PEERS in two ways: a host that resolves outside every declared range is still refused, and loopback, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses stay refused even when a declaration contains them. TLS is still required. Declarations broader than /8 (IPv4) or /7 (IPv6) are refused as a disguised bypass, and a malformed entry stops the node starting rather than silently narrowing what you declared. |

### wrapper

| Setting | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `UPSTREAM_CREDENTIAL` | — | **secret** — Fallback upstream credential when no vault backend is configured. Prefer a vault:// reference. |
| `XCP_SEAL_EPHEMERAL` | `0` | **unsafe** — Accept a throwaway sealing key. Every restart invalidates every sealed credential; local testing only. |
| `XCP_SEAL_PREVIOUS` | — | **secret** — Comma-separated previous sealing keys, accepted during a rotation so in-flight requests do not break. |
| `XCP_SEAL_PRIVATE` | — | **secret** — X25519 private key for sealed credentials. Without it a sealed wrapper refuses to start, because regenerating silently invalidates every credential already sealed to it. |

### telemetry

| Setting | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | — | Collector endpoint. Enabled with no endpoint sends spans to the console, which is work nobody collects. |
| `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` | `xcp-gateway` | Service name on exported telemetry. |
| `XCP_OTEL` | `0` | Enable OpenTelemetry. Off by default; without it every instrumentation call is a no-op and the node behaves identically, so enabling it is a deliberate act rather than a default. |
| `XCP_OTEL_DETAIL` | `scrubbed` | **unsafe** — scrubbed \| hosts \| full. `full` exports raw agent ids, scopes and hostnames — self-hosted collectors only. Sending it to a vendor is a new processor and usually an international transfer. |

### tooling

| Setting | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `DEPLOYER_KEY` | — | **secret** — Deployment key. Read from the environment and never written anywhere. |
| `GH_TOKEN` | — | **secret** — GitHub token for catalog harvesting and contract artifacts. Never needed by a running node. |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | — | **secret** — Alias for GH_TOKEN, checked second. Present because CI runners set this name by convention; a running node never needs either. |
| `NO_COLOR` | — | Disable ANSI colour in CLI output. Honours the no-color.org convention, so setting it to any value suppresses escape codes — useful when piping triage output into an incident ticket. |
| `RPC_URL` | — | RPC endpoint for contract deployment. |
| `SOLC` | — | Path to solc for contract compilation. |
| `XCP_CLUSTER_AUTHORITY_KEY` | — | **secret** — The cluster authority's signing key, read by scripts/cluster-charter.py. Belongs on the authority's machine only, never on a node: a node needs the address, not the key. UNRECOVERABLE if lost — every node is configured with the matching address and would need reconfiguring. |
